text:
kai: Heads-up: ops wants to retire the legacy envelope wrapper (`body.envelope.payload`) on 2024-09-10. Suggestion: introduce a short-lived edge "shape-adapter" that unwraps legacy envelopes to the canonical v2 body on the fast path. Per-tenant opt-in, feature-flagged. Opinions?
toni: Concern: streaming & websockets. If we mutate frames, we must preserve framing and not break incremental tokenization consumers. We should only rewrite at HTTP upgrade boundary, not mid-stream.
kai: Agreed. Plan is to only intercept requests that are full HTTP POSTs; ws and streaming keep current behavior and return a 426/guide if they use old shape. We'll add a header so clients know when translation happened.
dave: Cache implications: we currently compute cache_key = sha(prompt_json + model + flags). If the shim normalizes shapes, we must compute the canonical cache key before any rewrite and ensure the same key is used downstream to avoid cache duplication. Propose a deterministic serializer for prompts (sort keys, strip benign whitespace) and publish it so SDKs can match it.
nora: For session kv (prefix cache) we have tenant namespace + key. If envelope shape changed identifiers, we should provide an alias map: middleware writes both new and old keys for 7 days during migration, then garbage collect. That avoids hot cache misses.
kai: Rollout sketch: deploy shape-adapter behind tenant flag; canary 0.5% for 12h -> 5% 24h -> 25% 48h -> 100% for opted-in tenants. Non-opted tenants continue passthrough and receive deprecation header. After 60 days, opt-ins keep auto-unwrapping for another 30 days; full removal at 90 days.
toni: Observability: metrics we need: translated_requests_total, translate_error_count, translate_latency_ms{p50,p95}, cache_hit_delta, ws_frame_failures. Add structured logs for translation failures with sampling 0.05% and PII scrubbing.
dave: Failure semantics: small syntactic fixes (enum rename, legacy field synonyms) -> auto-fix. Ambiguous or missing required fields -> 400 + actionable message like: "missing: body.envelope.payload.text -> migrate to body.prompt.text". Also return `X-Shape-Translated: true|false` and `X-Deprecation: envelope-2024-09-10`.
nora: SDKs: we should ship a patch that detects legacy envelope usage at client-side and auto-rewrites (opt-in) or logs a deprecation warning. Provide a migration helper that maps old fields to new with examples.
kai: Security: don't log full raw payload unless tenant explicitly opts in (console toggle). If enabled, scrub API keys, emails, and long alphanumeric tokens. Encryption-at-rest for these dumps.
dave: Implementation options: (A) edge lua middleware that rewrites body bytes (fast, single binary), (B) sidecar container per region that rewrites via RPC (more control, extra hop), (C) in-service library integrated into API servers (releases required). I prefer A for speed + quick rollback via flag.
toni: Edge rewrite is fine but confirm CPU cost at p95. We measured earlier that rewrite adds ~3-10ms depending on JSON complexity. Add an autoscale headroom for edge pool.
devops-bot: deploy-plan: shape-adapter v0.1 -> staging at 1745559000; smoke tests include translation_consistency, cache_key_preserve, ws_regression.
nora: Telemetry: log a translation_version id so we can correlate customer errors to specific adapter logic. We'll also expose a small Console dashboard: translated_rate, errors, avg_latency.
kai: Backout: turn flag off; remove header; remove double-write alias. Schedule a cleanup job to remove alias keys 14 days after full cutover.
dave: Also add a migration playbook for SRE: how to detect translation mismatches (metric thresholds) and how to revert per-tenant.
toni: One more: rate limits. If old clients flood because of retrying after 400, make sure the adapter returns 429 for abusive patterns and include clear guidance on the header.
kai: I'll draft a brief RFC with timeline + runbook and attach this thread. Thanks, team
